stops.note: 'knot'; usually traced to the Varangian Norsemen who helped found the Rus' state from the 800s
a knotted leather whip; Peter the Great's son Alexei died in 1718 after being beaten with it on his father's orders
English kept the French spelling; the knout stayed a byword for tsarist cruelty even after Nicholas I abolished it as a judicial punishment in 1845

current_meaning: a whip formerly used to flog criminals in Russia
